title: The Collections Framework
summary: The interfaces and implementations of java.util - List, Set, Map, Queue and Deque with ArrayList, LinkedList, HashSet, LinkedHashSet, TreeSet, HashMap, LinkedHashMap, TreeMap, ArrayDeque and PriorityQueue - choosing between them, iterating, counting and grouping with maps, the equals and hashCode contract, and immutable collections.

cards.q: Which set keeps its items sorted?
cards.a:
`TreeSet`

`TreeSet` keeps its items in sorted order. `HashSet` has no useful order, and `LinkedHashSet` keeps the order the items were first added.

Puts 1 if `word` is not yet a key, otherwise adds 1 to its current value

`merge` stores the given value for a new key; for an existing key it combines the old value and the given one with the function, here `Integer::sum`. That makes it the one-line way to count.

cards.q: A class overrides `equals` but not `hashCode`, and two equal objects are added to a `HashSet`. How many items does the set hold?
cards.a:
Probably 2, because their hash codes differ

`HashSet` looks in the bucket for the hash code first; with different hash codes, `equals` is never even asked.
